extracted.intended_audience: licensed individual customs brokers; CBP-selected accreditors; continuing education providers; U.S. Customs and Border Protection staff
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule establishing a continuing education framework that requires individual licensed customs brokers to complete and certify qualified continuing broker education credits, and sets standards for accreditation, providers, recordkeeping, and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability — individual brokers only
rubrics_metrics.description: The continuing education requirement applies to 'individual brokers' (licensed individuals) and not to the entire licensed body of customs brokers (which includes partnerships, associations, corporations). The rule uses the term 'individual brokers' in §§ 111.0, 111.1, 111.101–111.104 to make clear who is affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The continuing education requirement only applies to persons holding an individual customs broker license. Interpretations, exemptions, and certification obligations discussed throughout the rule are directed to individual brokers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required credits — 36 credits per triennial period
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual brokers are required to complete at least 36 continuing education credits per three-year triennial period to administratively maintain their license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP determined 36 credits over three years is a reasonable expectation of someone with a Federal professional license. CBP will provide free qualified continuing education to help cover required credits; private offerings also may be accredited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smallest unit of credit — half credits allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule allows recognition of 'half credits' (30 minutes of continuous participation) as the smallest unit of continuing education credit; previously the NPRM proposed one credit per hour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP will count one hour = one credit and allow 0.5-credit (30 minutes) increments; training providers and recordkeeping should reflect this unit granularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triennial cycle timing and certification date
rubrics_metrics.description: The 36-month continuing education cycle begins February 1 and ends January 31 every three years. Individual brokers must certify completion of required continuing education with the filing of their triennial status reports (due beginning mid-December through end of February, per 19 U.S.C. 1641(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation on or before the last day of January counts for that cycle; participation after the last day of January counts for the next triennial period. Brokers may file triennial reports early but must ensure the required credits were completed in the shortened timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: No carryover of excess credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual brokers may not carry over continuing education credits completed in excess of the 36-credit requirement from one triennial period to the next.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP will not allow carryover because the requirement is meant to ensure training within a recent (three-year) period and maintain an up-to-date knowledge base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial certification/proration for first cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: For the triennial period beginning Feb 1, 2024, CBP will reduce the 36-credit requirement by six credits for approximately every six months that elapse between Feb 1, 2024 and the compliance date announced in a subsequent Federal Register notice. The first time individual brokers must certify compliance is with their 2027 triennial status reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP will announce the compliance date and the date on which qualified continuing broker education courses will be available at least 30 days before compliance; trainings completed before the announced compliance date will not qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified continuing broker education — accreditation or CBP identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualified continuing broker education consists of trainings and educational activities that have been accredited by a CBP-selected accreditor or identified by CBP per § 111.103(a). When offered by a government agency, CBP will identify the specific qualified opportunities relevant to customs business that may provide credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only CBP-identified or CBP-selected-accreditor-accredited activities count. CBP will publish CBP-identified trainings and the list of CBP-selected accreditors on CBP.gov to enable brokers to find qualified offerings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognized categories of trainings and activities
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP recognizes multiple categories of trainings/educational activities for credit; the final rule amends the first category (seminars, webinars, workshops) and adds a fifth category allowing self-guided trainings/educational activities which culminate in a retention test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the NPRM proposed four broad categories, the final rule (as described) expands/clarifies categories to include: (1) seminars/webinars/workshops (amended description), (2–4) other structured categories proposed in the NPRM, and (5) self-guided trainings with a retention test. Providers and accreditors should map offerings to these categories per §111.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of government-offered trainings
rubrics_metrics.description: When qualified continuing broker education is offered by a government agency (including CBP), CBP will identify specific opportunities (after consultation where appropriate) that are relevant to customs business and may provide continuing education credit upon completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP will list government-offered qualifying trainings on CBP.gov; CBP intends to provide free online modules and in-person events sufficient to cover the 36-credit requirement for brokers who rely on CBP offerings.

rubrics_metrics.name: CBP-selected accreditors — selection and role
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP will select accreditors via SAM using an RFI and RFP process. CBP-selected accreditors will consider trainings and educational activities for accreditation and work with CBP to establish standards/guidelines for qualified continuing broker education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP will announce CBP-selected accreditors on CBP.gov. Accreditors will apply CBP-established standards when accrediting private-sector offerings and will maintain processes consistent with CBP guidance in §111.103(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accreditor prohibition on denial based solely on prior denial
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP will explicitly prohibit CBP-selected accreditors from denying accreditation to a training or educational activity solely because it was previously denied by that CBP-selected accreditor or any other CBP-selected accreditor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accreditors must consider each accreditation application on its merits and may not summarily deny accreditation solely due to a prior denial by any CBP-selected accreditor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards and quality safeguards for private-sector offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP will work with CBP-selected accreditors to create standards that ensure robust and diverse private-sector education offerings and include safeguards that guarantee individual brokers receive the requisite level of quality in private offerings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards/guidelines will be established jointly with accreditors and published; they are intended to prevent monopolies, ensure diversity of content and quality, and provide brokers meaningful choices for meeting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping — maintenance and retention period
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual brokers must maintain their own records of completed continuing broker education and certify completion with their triennial status report. Records of continuing education must be retained for three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP will maintain a central location on CBP.gov for identifying qualified trainings. CBP may request records (CBP assumes it will randomly select a sample, e.g., 10% in its analysis) and will only begin record requests after the first triennial period during which the rule is in effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification method — triennial status report filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual brokers must certify compliance with the continuing broker education requirement as part of filing their triennial status reports pursuant to 19 U.S.C. 1641(g) and 19 CFR 111.30(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification aligns the reporting and education requirements to simplify administrative burden; brokers should ensure certifications reflect their maintained records and accredited trainings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions and waivers for newly licensed brokers
rubrics_metrics.description: Newly licensed individual brokers receive a waiver of the continuing broker education requirement for the triennial period in which they receive their licenses (see §111.102(a)(2)). Brokers who have not yet completed a triennial status report are exempt from continuing education until after their first triennial status report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recognizes the recency of licensing exam knowledge and avoids immediate burden; affected brokers should consult §111.102 for details on timing and application of the waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement — audits, suspension, revocation, penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to comply with certification or record requests may result in enforcement actions consistent with statutory authority (including suspension or revocation of license under 19 U.S.C. 1641 and other remedies). CBP will include details of enforcement in §111.104 and related sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP's analysis anticipates record requests and possible corrective actions; brokers failing to maintain or produce required records may face license suspension and related costs to regain compliance or reapply for a license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility — broker topic choice and delivery formats
rubrics_metrics.description: The framework is intended to be flexible: individual brokers may choose trainings and topics relevant to their practice areas and are not required to attend uniform mandatory monthly sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP judged flexibility important because brokers specialize in areas; CBP will provide a range of public and private offerings to accommodate differing needs and geographies (including online modules for remote brokers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on CBP-conflict-of-interest / free baseline offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: CBP will continue to provide free online modules and workshops so brokers have a baseline option to satisfy continuing education and to avoid creating a private-sector monopoly that profits from the requirement; CBP does not intend to financially profit from the requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBP will publish enough free accredited or CBP-identified options so individual brokers can meet the requirement without incurring prohibitive costs.
